overview_raw: The Essentials of Data Networks Microcredential provides a high-level understanding of networking for anyone interested in an IT or related Career. Network administrator, data centre or Web operator, or a computer network technician are entry level careers graduates of this program can choose to pursue. Delivery: online. See details . The emphasis in this microcredential is on networking knowledge with several basic skills that are useful for a home or Small Office/Home Office (SOHO) network. Next up Entrance Requirements
entrance_requirements_raw: About Flexible Learning Flexible Learning offers a variety of courses and programs in different delivery modes and locations to customize your learning at your own pace. You can review course prerequisites on our website and if you meet them, you’ll be able to register for that available course immediately. Some courses may require departmental approval or formal acceptance into the program. BCIT Flexible Learning courses are offered during the Winter (January), Spring/Summer (April), and Fall (September) terms. Scheduled intakes Ongoing Flexible Learning (Part-time Studies) intakes: January, April, and September . Application processing Ongoing throughout the year. Entrance requirements Successful completion of Grade 10. Recommended for success Students should have a general knowledge of how to operate a computer and browse the internet. International applicants This program is available to international applicants who will complete the program from outside Canada or who currently have a valid status in Canada other than study permit. Study permit: International applicants accepted into this program are not eligible for a study permit. Apply to program Formal application to the microcredential is not required. Upon successful completion of the courses , email the program contact with your full name, student number, and mailing address to be issued a microcredential. courses.course_overview_raw: ​In this course, students will learn about communications in a connected world. Students will identify network devices and connections then install a simulation tool to allow further exploration of networks. After building a simple network, students will examine network protocols and will delve into the concepts behind network design. Prerequisite(s): Completion of Grade 10 or equivalent

In this course, students will learn about Internet Protocol (IP) and how routing works between networks. Students will create a fully connected network and will subnet an IP address. Students will learn about IP address management and how Dynamic Addressing occurs using Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP). Finally, students will create Domain Name System (DNS) records in a Domain Name Server.​ Prerequisite(s): 50% in XINC 1101

​Building on previous work, this course will apply that learning to a home-office network. Students will set up a home router and add devices to a home network. They will implement security on the home network including a firewall and wireless authentication.​ Prerequisite(s): 50% in XINC 1102
